# Finite-element audit for incompressible free surfaces

Reviewed 25 November 2026 at commit `4510bb8aec481e33a2afb6434759c86e2946815c`. The inventory covers every file under `Code/Source/solver/FE`. Physics and Application sources are cited where they establish which equations, benchmarks or outputs use an FE operation. The later tracker revision `fc0bde198678` supplied the fitted-wave measurements cited here. Its only changed file was the tracker. The reviewed solver sources and benchmark generators are identical at both revisions.

At the audited revision, a 32-step capillary-wave run accepted one step after kinematic reconciliation exhausted all eight iterations. The area change exceeded the reported kinematic target by **1.20421 × 10⁻⁶**. Five hydrostatic tank runs on the same executable preserved height and volume through 100 steps each. The review also reproduced a pressure time-labeling error in first-order generalized-α and three pressure-control failures on cut tetrahedra.

**Original audit status.** All 26 original findings, A01–A26, are resolved. Work continues on the later audit findings.

## Resolution of the first four findings

**A01 · Accepted interface volume.** Reconciliation evaluates the FE velocity on each cut, accounts for the actual swept area or volume, and measures the flux again on the returned interface. Limiting can move a blocked share to admissible nodes on the same connected cut. The timestep controller can reject an infeasible endpoint before advancing history. In a regression, it rejected Δt = 0.2 and accepted two steps of 0.1 with the original sharp volume. Subsequent patch bounds and redistancing also check the physical budget before publication. The analytic P2 triangle gives an interface flux of 9/16. On the original 32-step L64 wave, independent integration of the saved velocity and level-set fields recovered the original 1.20421 × 10⁻⁶ area defect and measured a maximum below 2 × 10⁻¹⁶ after the repair. [Reconciliation](../Code/Source/solver/FE/LevelSet/LevelSetKinematicReconciliation.cpp) · [Acceptance and redistancing tests](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Tests/Unit/LevelSet/test_LevelSetKinematicReconciliation.cpp) · [Timestep rejection and retry](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Tests/Unit/TimeStepping/test_TimeLoopConvergence.cpp)

The L16, L32, and L64 waves each completed four periods at the stock timestep and passed the spatial frequency, damping, and area-drift criteria. On L64, all 200 corrections converged and the largest stepwise budget defect was 9.15 × 10⁻¹⁶. Before the repair, 193 converged and the largest defect was 1.59 × 10⁻⁶. The computed normal velocity has a small net flux. The maximum relative area drift over the four periods was 2.69 × 10⁻⁶ after the repair and 2.07 × 10⁻⁶ before it. Both are within the benchmark limit of 10⁻⁴. [Wave generator](../tests/cases/fluid/free_surface_benchmarks/capillary_wave_2d/generate_case.py) · [Benchmark criteria](../tests/cases/fluid/free_surface_benchmarks/capillary_wave_2d/tolerances.json)

**A02 · Endpoint pressure.** First-order generalized-α reconstructs fluid pressure from its converged stage value and the previous endpoint. The fluid formulation declares pressure by field ID, including renamed fields and the pressures of both phases. Traction and stage observers still use the solve time. For a fluid starting at rest without a supplied pressure field, compatible uniform outlet or exterior free-surface data can supply the initial pressure. In the pipe test a 1,000-unit shift of outlet pressure produces the same shift throughout the fluid at step four. The natural-traction Stokes test checks both clocks through a rejected step, a shorter retry, and continuation. In the time-dependent manufactured cut problem, halving Δt from 0.1 to 0.05 to 0.025 gave endpoint pressure L² errors of 0.002608, 0.0006601, and 0.0001662. Native continuation data for this interpolation contain physical endpoint pressure. [Time integration](../Code/Source/solver/FE/TimeStepping/TimeLoop.cpp) · [Pressure-clock and startup tests](../Code/Source/solver/Physics/Tests/Unit/test_NavierStokesPressureGauge.cpp) · [Outlet-pressure test](../Code/Source/solver/Application/Tests/Unit/test_OutletModelAccuracy.cpp)

**A03 · Contact-line velocity.** A crossing exactly at a wall vertex receives one tangential velocity constraint. The two wall neighbors establish whether the phases cross there. The triangle containing the outgoing zero contour supplies the contact angle, including when another MPI rank owns it. Tangencies and intervals of zero level set give no isolated contact point. A branching contour has no unique contact angle and is reported as such. The Ren–E verifier measures the same angle from the saved interface geometry. The kinked two-rank case gives a signed speed of 0.599503719021. Five serial tests, three two-rank tests, and 16 benchmark tests cover both crossing directions and the degenerate cases. [Strong contact law](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Constraints/ContactPointVelocityConstraint.cpp) · [MPI regression](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Tests/Unit/Constraints/test_ContactPointVelocityConstraintMPI.cpp) · [Ren–E measurement](../tests/cases/fluid/free_surface_benchmarks/ren_e_2d/verify.py)

**A04 · Cut-tetrahedron pressure control.** On a tetrahedral mesh restricted to a level-set phase, the divergence stabilization now uses the sum of squared physical gradients of the four parent barycentric coordinates. This gives a single length scale across cut and fully wet parents in the phase. The momentum and pressure-gradient terms retain the unit-determinant simplex metric. The original fixed-cut test now reaches 0.498063 and the moving-cut test reaches 0.490827 against a minimum of 0.45. The three-mesh spread is 1.67093 against a maximum of 1.75. A separate assembled-work regression checks the coefficient on an anisotropic cut tetrahedron with each vertex as reference origin. [VMS formulation](../Code/Source/solver/Physics/Formulations/NavierStokes/IncompressibleNavierStokesVMSModule.cpp) · [Cut and refinement criteria](../Code/Source/solver/Physics/Tests/Unit/test_FreeSurfaceCutStability.cpp) · [Assembled-work regression](../Code/Source/solver/Physics/Tests/Unit/test_NavierStokesVMSManufactured.cpp)

The stabilization has a measurable tradeoff. In the manufactured traction-driven Stokes problem at mesh spacing 0.25, Δt = 0.025, and cut height 0.70, the endpoint velocity L² error fell from 0.01310 to 0.01030 and the stage pressure L² error fell from 0.00619 to 0.00521. The divergence L² norm rose from 0.03482 to 0.04050. The other three cut heights, 0.55, 0.755, and 0.85, showed the same direction of change. At mesh spacing 0.125, velocity and pressure errors were 0.00161 and 0.000862. On the affine patch all three norms were below 10⁻¹⁵. [Manufactured problem and measurement protocol](free_surface_program_tracker.md#L2368)

**Verification on 25 November 2026.** All 93 configured native CTest entries passed, including the three previously failing Physics shards and the one-, two-, and four-rank free-surface comparison. All 60 Python tests for the capillary-wave, hydrostatic-tank, and Ren–E benchmarks passed. Five 2D and 3D tanks held their interface height and liquid volume through 100 steps each. In a separate tank with no initial pressure array, all wet-support vertices had pressure 37 in each of four saved outputs on both one and two ranks. Two older WP7 Python checks still failed on the original and updated source trees. They check the literal CMake spelling of an MPI registration and the spelling of a metadata property writer. [Hydrostatic benchmark](../tests/cases/fluid/free_surface_benchmarks/tank_at_rest/verify.py) · [WP7 source checks](../tests/test_free_surface_wp7_cut_stability_qualification_runner.py)

## Resolution of A05–A08

**A05 · Ambiguous quadrilateral cuts.** The `LinearCorner` cutter represents one segment per quadrilateral. It now counts the distinct boundary crossings before merging nearby points and reports unsupported topology when a cell needs multiple branches. For φ = xy − 0.2 on [−1,1]², the previous negative area was 2.270270270, while independent integration gives 3.043775165. Callers now receive a diagnostic before either side publishes an area. Tests cover rotated and reflected cells, both signs, the exact saddle, near-saddle cuts, and two-crossing controls. A failed refresh preserves the previous snapshot. Both ranks receive the failure when only one owns the saddle cell. [Cutter](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Interfaces/LevelSetInterfaceBuilder.cpp) · [Snapshot and volume regressions](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Tests/Unit/LevelSet/test_LevelSetVolume.cpp) · [Two-rank regression](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Tests/Unit/LevelSet/test_LevelSetVolumeMPI.cpp)

**A06 · Moving cut-surface traction.** The generated `LinearCorner` rule retains its isovalue and the ordered parent edges where the level set crosses. The differentiated assembly moves those intersections and the quadrature points they define. It differentiates the mapped surface normal and integration weight at each point. On the unit tetrahedron with φ = x − 1/4 the assembled residual is 9/32. A uniform increment of φ gives a tangent of 0.75, matching the centered difference from freshly cut surfaces. A fixed ordering of the four crossed edges keeps the triangulation of a tetrahedral cut stable as the interface moves. A cut through a vertex, a rule whose normals were replaced by a higher-order evaluator, or a rule without the edge data reports that its derivative is unavailable. Field gradients on a 2D parent use its x–y chart and require a nonsingular projection onto that plane. Independent centered recuts on planar and curved parents checked 4,032 matrix entries at each of three perturbation sizes. The largest absolute error at ε = 10⁻⁵ was 5.04 × 10⁻¹⁰, including spatial pressure loads, the positive trace and a nonconstant field from the previous timestep. [Surface differential](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Forms/CutSurfaceGeometry.cpp) · [Regenerated-quadrature tests](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Tests/Unit/Forms/test_CutCellForms.cpp)

**A07 · Internal-interface parent volume.** Both phase traces now use the physical measure of the full parent cell when evaluating hₙ = 2V/A. On the unit tetrahedron the translated-cut tests recover ∫Γ hₙ = 1/3, including the quarter cut that previously returned 0.5625. Scaling the tetrahedron by three gives 9. A trapezoid with a varying Jacobian independently verifies parent area 2.5, cut length 2.25 and hₙ = 5/2.25. [Generated-interface assembly](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Assembly/StandardAssembler.cpp) · [Parent-measure regressions](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Tests/Unit/Assembly/test_StandardAssembler.cpp)

**A08 · Curved fitted normals.** The fitted weak form and the boundary functional use the reference outward covector mapped by the inverse-transpose Jacobian. For F(r,s) = (r,s + 2r²), the top midpoint now has normal +eᵧ and signed curvature −4. The closed integral of nᵧ is zero, and the assembled vertical pressure force for p = y is −4, equal to minus the cell area. The same transform preserves normals under reversed numbering and retains positive face areas after a change of length units. The separate retained-cut and trace scale checks in [A14](#a14) remain open. [Fitted geometry](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Geometry/FrameGeometry.cpp) · [Weak-form pressure load](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Tests/Unit/Systems/test_InterfaceOrientation.cpp) · [Boundary functional tests](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Tests/Unit/Assembly/test_FunctionalAssembler.cpp)

**Verification on 25 November 2026.** All 93 configured native CTest entries passed, including the two- and four-rank runs. All 87 Python tests for the fitted drop, fitted wave, two-fluid hydrostatics, pressure jump and viscous jump passed. The modified solver passed all 12 two-fluid hydrostatic cases and all 204 comparisons between phase reversals. The benchmark runner recorded `DEVELOPMENT_PASS` for the uncommitted source tree. [Hydrostatic matrix](../tests/cases/fluid/free_surface_wp10_two_fluid_hydrostatic_matrix.json) · [Qualification runner](../tests/cases/fluid/run_free_surface_wp10_two_fluid_hydrostatic_qualification.py).

## Resolution of A09–A11

**A09 · Inhomogeneous multipoint constraints.** The DOF assembler represents each local unknown as a row of the prolongation P plus its prescribed offset g. The joint assembly computes PᵀAP and Pᵀ(b − Ag) for free, fixed and multipoint-constrained DOFs. An unresolved chain reports the two DOFs and requires closure before the element or batch can write. The audit case x = (y, y + 1), A = I, b = 0 gives stiffness 2 and load −1. A nonsymmetric case with chained masters gives stiffness rows (14.5, −11) and (−15, 30), and load (−30.25, 81.5). Regression tests also exercise separate matrix and load assembly, small master weights and rescaling. [Assembly](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Dofs/ConstrainedAssembly.cpp) · [Constraint closure](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Dofs/DofConstraints.cpp) · [Tests](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Tests/Unit/Dofs/test_ConstrainedAssembly.cpp)

**A10 · Constraint interpolation weights.** The helper now evaluates the FE nodal basis for the requested topology, nodal family and field degree. The degree-two triangle returns six weights, with (1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0) at the first vertex. Tests check node ordering, partition of unity and affine reproduction, including reduced quadratic cells and fields whose degree differs from the geometry. The edge midpoint constraint uses the same basis when all parent nodal DOFs are supplied and retains linear midpoint interpolation for two supplied vertices. The source search found no production free-surface caller. [Interpolation](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Constraints/ConstraintTools.cpp) · [Tests](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Tests/Unit/Constraints/test_ConstraintTools.cpp)

**A11 · Missing owned matrix coefficients.** FSILS and Trilinos check each nonzero contribution against the owned matrix graph. A missing slot reports the global row, column and coefficient. Both backends validate the entire element before writing it. Worker threads record failures for finalization, and distributed finalization reports the same failure on all participating ranks. In the constraint test, activating the master in x₁ = ½x₂ requires two new couplings. The stale graph rejects the write. After rebuilding, the reduced matrix has rows (4, 2.5) and (3, 2), and its product with (1, 1) is (6.5, 5). Exact zeros in absent slots are accepted. A two-rank advancing Ren–E case completed all 12 steps with two aggregation refreshes and five constraint-fill refreshes. [FSILS implementation](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Backends/FSILS/FsilsMatrix.cpp) · [Distributed FSILS tests](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Tests/Unit/Backends/test_FsilsBackendMPI.cpp) · [Trilinos tests](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Tests/Unit/Backends/test_TrilinosMatrixAssembly.cpp)

**Verification on 25 November 2026.** All 93 configured native CTest entries passed, including 33 MPI and 10 free-surface entries. All 110 tests in the optional DOF module passed. An independent comparison with dense condensation matched 26,884 entries across 900 systems. The Trilinos 13.2 backend passed the serial solve tests, including algebraic multigrid with GCC 14.2, and all six matrix tests on two MPI ranks. Two-rank checks also propagated the error on both FSILS and Tpetra when core FE MPI support was disabled. [DOF regression cases](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Tests/Unit/Dofs/test_ConstrainedAssembly.cpp) · [Trilinos solver tests](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Tests/Unit/Backends/test_LinearSolverConformance_Trilinos.cpp)

The solver’s FSILS assembly path with precomputed entry locations had similar before-and-after timings in a local microbenchmark. The public direct block helper resolved and checked the full block before writing and took about twice as long for the tested blocks of four and eight nodes with four DOFs per node. The repository search found only test callers for that helper.

## Further resolutions of the original findings

**A12 · Distributed PETSc nullspaces.** The solver creates each mode with the matrix's domain layout, orthonormalizes the modes on the matrix communicator and checks that the operator annihilates them. It projects the solution onto the requested gauge. Nested systems receive their modes in global field order. PETSc matrices now install the declared CSR columns before locking the sparsity pattern. In PETSc 3.18.5 Release, the gauged solves matched the prescribed solutions and produced residual norms below 10⁻¹¹. Tests ran on one, two and three ranks, including an empty partition and a configuration supplied on only one rank. [PETSc solver](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Backends/PETSc/PetscLinearSolver.cpp) · [Distributed regression](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Tests/Unit/Backends/test_PetscNullspaceMPI.cpp)

**A13 · Structural rank of an auxiliary DAE step.** The analyzer computes a maximum row-column matching on the nonzero pattern of the evaluated step Jacobian, Fₓ + αFẋ. Backward Euler uses the local step size. Other integrators can supply their rate coefficient. Metadata-only analysis leaves the rank unevaluated. The audit's three-row counterexample now reports structural rank two. The rate-only equation has rank one for an implicit step. A test with identical numerical rows and a full matching verifies the distinction between structural and numerical rank. All 451 auxiliary tests passed. [DAE analyzer](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Auxiliary/AuxiliaryDAEAnalyzer.cpp) · [Regression tests](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Tests/Unit/Auxiliary/test_AuxiliaryStateModel.cpp)

**A14 · Scale-independent element and trace geometry.** Retained-volume mapping, scalar measures, trace gradients and fitted surface transformations now test degeneracy using normalized Jacobian columns or tangents. On a tetrahedron of side 10⁻⁵, the retained weight is h³/48 and the trace gradient of the physical x coordinate is (1,0,0). At side 10⁻⁸ the fitted coordinate-face area is h²/2. Collinear and coplanar frames still fail the degeneracy check. Scaling each Jacobian column by a power of two preserves the exact cofactor cancellations used in the manufactured-channel trace certificate. The aggregation test verifies the same exact extension weights at three translated placements and requires a guarded round-off acceptance among them. [Geometry implementation](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Geometry/FrameGeometry.cpp) · [Trace tests](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Tests/Unit/Geometry/test_CutInterfaceFieldEvaluation.cpp) · [Retained measures](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Tests/Unit/Geometry/test_GeneratedActiveBoundaryDomain.cpp)

**A15 · Affine geometry and the Hex27 Jacobian cache.** For nodal bases with known linear precision, the mapping compares every geometry coefficient with an affine map in coordinates relative to the first node. Other bases use pointwise evaluation. On the audit's Hex27 polynomial all eight quadrature determinants agree with the analytic Jacobian. The regression also checks affine cells, a reversed coordinate direction and a rescaling by 10⁻⁶. [Affine predicate](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Geometry/IsoparametricMapping.cpp) · [Hex27 regression](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Tests/Unit/Geometry/test_IsoparametricMapping.cpp)

**A16 · Geometry order on Hex20, Wedge15 and Pyramid13.** The default mapping uses the mesh geometry order and the corresponding basis, including midside nodes. Callers can select order one for a vertex-only map, including when updating its coordinates. For manufactured maps with unchanged vertices, volume assembly and the independent fitted boundary integral of z n_z both give 8.8 on Hex20, 1.05 on Wedge15 and 4/3 − 0.3 on Pyramid13. The order-one controls give 8, 1 and 4/3. All 355 geometry tests passed. [Mapping factory](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Geometry/MappingFactory.cpp) · [Curved geometry tests](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Tests/Unit/Geometry/test_HigherOrderMappings.cpp)

**A17 · Projection and Jacobian cache identity.** Scalar projections retain the tabulation for their actual basis and quadrature points. The public scalar cache view also owns its tabulation across cache clears. In both warm-up orders the Lagrange and Bernstein projections of x² now return 0.0625 at x = ¼. The Jacobian cache assigns generations to mapping instances and checks the saved node coordinates when reusing entries. Linear and isoparametric tetrahedra now update the cached determinant from 1 to 2 on a node reset. Constructing another mapping at the same address gives the new determinant of 3. [Projection](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Spaces/FunctionSpace.cpp) · [Jacobian cache](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Geometry/JacobianCache.cpp) · [Projection regression](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Tests/Unit/Spaces/test_SpaceCacheWorkspace.cpp) · [Mapping regression](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Tests/Unit/Geometry/test_JacobianCacheGeometryQuadrature.cpp)

**A18 · Physical Hessians on curved cells and facets.** The functional assembler uses the same inverse-map second derivatives as the standard assembler. The transformation also applies to secondary scalar and component fields and to batched functionals. Tests recover zero Hessians for the physical coordinates on a curved Tetra10 and the analytic Hessians and Laplacians of y + kx² on a curved Quad9 and its fitted faces. [Functional assembler](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Assembly/FunctionalAssembler.cpp) · [Curved-cell and facet tests](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Tests/Unit/Assembly/test_FunctionalAssembler.cpp)

**A19 · Matrix-free actions and residuals.** The matrix-free cell operator shares the standard assembler's geometry, basis and orientation transforms. Trial and test spaces may have different maps and dimensions. An affine constraint lifts the current state for a residual and uses its homogeneous part for a tangent action. Independent comparisons with assembled systems cover a 16-by-32 mixed block, a 12-component tetrahedron, nonlinear residuals and tangents, and oriented H(div) and H(curl) bases. All 42 focused checks passed across 15 repetitions with four OpenMP threads. [Matrix-free assembler](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Assembly/MatrixFreeAssembler.cpp) · [Assembly regressions](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Tests/Unit/Assembly/test_MatrixFreeAssembler.cpp)

**A20 · Symmetric eigenvalues and their derivatives.** The eigensolver scales its inputs and resolves close roots in the shifted matrix. The spectral Hessian uses eigenvalue gaps in the same scaled arithmetic. Against an independent Eigen reference, 7,200 comparisons from 10⁻²⁹⁰ to 10²⁹⁰ had maximum normalized eigenvalue error below 1.2 × 10⁻¹⁵. Another 600 comparisons sampled spectra up to 0.9999 times the largest finite double. A matrix with normalized roots −0.96, 0.93 and 0.93 now has a finite, accurate simple-root Hessian. The 22 native math and Forms checks cover rotated spectra and finite second derivatives at separated eigenvalues. [Eigensolver](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Math/Eigensolvers.h) · [Spectral derivative tests](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Tests/Unit/Forms/Tensor/test_SpectralEigenJIT.cpp)

**A21 · Vector transforms on embedded elements.** Piola values, ordinary vector gradients and fitted-edge frames now use the full physical embedding. Mesh-based H(div) and H(curl) spaces use the ambient dimension, and a type-only constructor can take it explicitly. Rotating a triangle from xy to xz preserves every entry of its Raviart–Thomas and Nédélec mass matrices for both volume and boundary assembly, with the interpreter and LLVM. Curved Piola values and ordinary gradients are covered. Requests for a curved Piola basis Jacobian still report the existing unsupported operation. All 16 extended LLVM parity cases passed with the Triangle6, Quad8 and Quad9 guard fixtures declaring their three-component embedding. The focused runs passed 352 geometry, 136 element, 192 space and 25 assembly tests. [Vector transforms](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Geometry/FrameAwareTransform.cpp) · [Assembly regression](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Tests/Unit/Assembly/test_StandardAssembler.cpp) · [Embedded geometry regressions](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Tests/Unit/Geometry/test_MetricSurfacePushForward.cpp)

**A22 · Composite refinement and position-based rule identity.** Tetrahedral refinement integrates over n³ child tetrahedra. Pyramid refinement subdivides the collapsed coordinates and includes the cross-section factor in the weight. Adaptive integration now reports the limit when successive refinements miss the requested tolerance. Position-based simplex rules report the degree they actually integrate, and distinct point locations retain distinct cache entries. All 73 focused tests passed, including the audit's quartic and nearly coincident point locations. [Composite quadrature](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Quadrature/CompositeQuadrature.cpp) · [Refinement tests](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Tests/Unit/Quadrature/test_CompositeAdaptiveSingularSurface.cpp) · [Position-based tests](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Tests/Unit/Quadrature/test_PositionBasedQuadrature.cpp)

**A23 · System-aware level-set volume diagnostics.** The diagnostics pass the system and complete solution to the volume evaluator, preserving the selected field, geometry and quadrature. Both public entry points use the same conversion to output scalars and reference losses. On a warped quadrilateral the generated negative area is 0.4, giving a loss of 0.1 from a reference of 0.5. On a quadratic field with positive values at every corner, diagnostics and direct generated quadrature agree on the area of the interior island. The serial level-set suite and the two- and four-rank level-set suites passed. [Diagnostics](../Code/Source/solver/FE/LevelSet/LevelSetDiagnostics.cpp) · [Volume regressions](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Tests/Unit/LevelSet/test_LevelSetVolume.cpp)

**A24 · Contact integration on fitted faces.** The penalty kernel obtains face points and physical integration weights from the common geometry evaluator at the mesh geometry order. A constant traction on reflected parallel solids now integrates to the analytic force on all eight tested faces across triangle, quadrilateral, tetrahedron, hexahedron, wedge and pyramid cells. The unit triangle edge and hexahedron face give magnitudes 1 and 4. All 11 focused contact checks passed. [Contact integration](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Systems/SurfaceContactKernel.cpp) · [Load regressions](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Tests/Unit/Systems/test_SurfaceContactKernel.cpp)

**A25 · Pointwise cut-interface normals in Forms.** `cutInterfaceNormal()` and the cut-cell terminal `interface_normal` read the physical normal at each quadrature point. `cutRuleNormal()` names the existing single normal stored with a rule, which existing callers can still request through `cutEmbeddedNormal()`. In a stretched cell with two distinct reference normals, interpreted and JIT forms reproduce the analytical y-flux 0.282842712474619. The constant rule normal gives zero. [Cut-cell terminals](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Forms/CutCellForms.h) · [Flux regression](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Tests/Unit/Forms/test_CutCellForms.cpp)

**A26 · Fitted ALE mesh velocity in VTK.** At accepted output times, the application writes the endpoint displacement rate. Generalized-alpha supplies its stored endpoint derivative and backward Euler uses the displacement increment over the accepted time step. On the fitted capillary wave the peak saved mesh speed was 0.001286450741. Across four outputs on one and two ranks, the maximum discrepancy from a displacement-history reconstruction was 8.1 × 10⁻¹⁸. Shared vertices agreed exactly between output pieces. A prescribed nonlinear displacement independently distinguishes the endpoint derivative from the step-average velocity. [Application writer](../Code/Source/solver/Application/Core/ApplicationDriver.cpp) · [On-disk output regression](../Code/Source/solver/Application/Tests/Support/ale_mesh_velocity_output.py)

## Further resolutions from the later audit

**A32 · History on a moving oblique wall.** The normal constraint now treats its master coefficients as time dependent when the mesh moves or the active boundary subset can change. The stage solution satisfies the current normal. Accepted states and rates retain the normal at their own time. In the unit-square test, shearing the wall to tangent (½,1) previously changed the accepted velocity from (0,1) to (½,1) and erased its derivative (½,0). Both histories are now preserved, while the current constraint gives the required x component ½. A fixed oblique reference wall still projects the derivative onto its constant tangent. All 20 serial constraint tests and all nine normal-constraint tests on each of two and four MPI ranks passed. [Normal constraint](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Constraints/NormalComponentConstraint.cpp) · [Moving-wall regression](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Tests/Unit/Systems/test_StrongDirichletConstraint.cpp)

**A33 · Retention of subdivided phase volumes.** The domain importer and geometry snapshot compare the total fraction of each phase in the parent cell with the retention threshold. In a Q2 strip, all eight individually small regions had been lost. Together they occupy a parent fraction of 2 × 10⁻⁸, above the default 10⁻⁸ cutoff. Both import paths now retain the full area of 7.999999996 × 10⁻⁸ and its one-sided interface. All 132 interface lifecycle tests and 82 snapshot and boundary tests passed, including the P1 one- and two-phase flux checks. [Parent-phase fractions](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Interfaces/LevelSetInterfaceDomain.h) · [Retention regressions](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Tests/Unit/LevelSet/test_LevelSetInterfaceLifecycle.cpp)

**A37 · Consistent startup rates with prescribed motion.** The generalized-α startup solve includes the free-row mass residual induced by a prescribed rate before eliminating constrained columns. For the tetrahedral mass equation 2ȧ + ḃ = 0 with b = t, the first endpoint now gives ȧ = −0.5 and a = −0.05. Previously it gave −0.6 and −0.04. On a Q1 quadrilateral, prescribing one corner rate of 1 produces rates of −½ at its edge neighbours and ¼ at the opposite corner. Disconnected cells on the other ranks retain zero rates. The quadrilateral check passed on one, two and four FSILS ranks, and all 346 enabled serial time-integration tests passed. [Startup assembly](../Code/Source/solver/FE/TimeStepping/TimeLoop.cpp) · [Tetrahedral mass equation](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Tests/Unit/TimeStepping/test_TimeLoopAcceptedState.cpp) · [Distributed mass equation](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Tests/Unit/Assembly/test_TimeLoopFsilsConvergenceMPI.cpp)

**A39 and A56 · Fitted mesh rollback after a rejected time step.** A time-step attempt snapshots native coordinates, the active configuration and the standard mesh-motion fields before any step callback. A rejection restores that state, its stored solutions and rates before the discard and rejection observers. Nonlinear iterations can commit their own coordinate updates within the attempt. On a fitted tetrahedron stretched by x = (1 + t)X, the rejected candidate reaches volume 1/5. The observer and retry now see the accepted volume 1/6 and mesh velocity 7. Previously they saw 1/5 and 9. The retried step commits 1/5 and 9. A throwing prescribed update also restores an existing coordinate buffer and configuration exactly. All 347 enabled time-integration tests passed, and the rank-local mesh rollback check passed on one, two and four MPI ranks. [Attempt rollback](../Code/Source/solver/FE/TimeStepping/TimeLoop.cpp) · [Mesh snapshot](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Systems/FESystem.cpp) · [Fitted rejection and retry](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Tests/Unit/TimeStepping/test_TimeLoopAcceptedState.cpp)

The experimental P2 simplex cutter now bounds the quadratic over each triangle or tetrahedron with its Bernstein coefficients before declaring it wholly on one side. It subdivides ambiguous bounds and reports an unresolved cut when it cannot certify the sign. A nearby strictly positive field still has zero negative measure. All 136 lifecycle tests passed. On a face shared by two quadrilaterals, the selected parent now contributes the interface exactly once and the touch-only policy emits no surface. A sign-reversed biquadratic field gave length 1, normal flux of opposite sign and the expected unit phase volumes in the snapshot. Two other tests distinguish a second interior root from a field strictly positive by 10⁻¹⁵ at the boundary. All 138 lifecycle tests and 123 geometry, snapshot and volume tests passed. On a quadratic triangle, the backend now also detects two crossings of a single edge in a mixed-sign child and clips both sides by the chord between the resolved roots. **A46 · Degenerate cut classifications.** The generated linear-corner rule now follows the direct volume evaluator's convention that values equal to the isovalue belong to the negative side. The kinematic flux, wall intersections and direct and generated volumes now share the same treatment of coefficients within the tolerance band. A stationary update preserves the supplied coefficients inside the band. All 77 serial regressions and three two-rank reconciliation tests passed. On the unit square it missed the integral of x²y⁶ by 1/8400. The new residual and tangent give the exact 1/21 to within 2 × 10⁻¹² for three triangle vertex orderings and the square, in the interpreter and LLVM. ## Findings on the free-surface path

<a id="a01"></a>

### A01. An unconverged kinematic correction can become the accepted interface

The unfitted one-phase profile enables kinematic reconciliation. The loop evaluates normal flux on one iterate, applies a vertex correction, then tests the update. On exhaustion the last pre-update flux supplies the target and the operation still sets its success flag. The maintenance pipeline commits on that flag. For a closed liquid without sources, the signed area or volume change must equal the time-integrated boundary flux within the stated tolerance on the **returned geometry**. [One-phase profile](../Code/Source/solver/Physics/Options/FreeSurfaceProfiles.cpp#L70) · [Reconciliation loop](../Code/Source/solver/FE/LevelSet/LevelSetKinematicReconciliation.cpp#L673) · [Final target and disposition](../Code/Source/solver/FE/LevelSet/LevelSetKinematicReconciliation.cpp#L980) · [Commit](../Code/Source/solver/FE/LevelSet/Maintenance/LevelSetMaintenancePipeline.cpp#L300)

| Witness | Expected | Observed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stock 2D capillary wave, L64, 32 accepted steps, one rank | The accepted liquid-area increment matches the trapezoidal kinematic target. | Step 15, Δt = 0.00797884560803, reported `applied=true`, `converged=false`, eight iterations. Area went from 0.5070702658822605 to 0.5070715138865349. Target increment 4.37954023935 × 10⁻⁸, actual increment 1.24800427448 × 10⁻⁶. |
| Unit P1 triangle, zero velocity, Δt = 0.05, accepted nodal φ = (−0.25, 0.75, −0.25), provisional φ = (−0.24, 0.55, −0.26) | Area stays 0.21875 with zero boundary flux. | Accepted correction gives 0.218755073252636 after eight iterations. |
| Unit triangle, φ = x − 1/4, P2 velocity (4y(1−y), 0) | The analytic interface flux is ∫₀³⁄⁴ 4y(1−y) dy = 9/16. | The reported flux is zero. The reconciliation path gathers only vertex velocities and interpolates between them. The P2 edge DOFs carry the entire signal. |

Evaluate the velocity trace at cut quadrature points through its actual FE space. Reevaluate flux and volume on the candidate that would be committed. Propagate an unsuccessful correction to the existing rejection/retry mechanism or return an explicitly accepted, quantified defect under a documented tolerance. A regression can check both zero- and nonzero-flux budgets, the restored pre-step state after rejection, and the independently measured area over the next accepted step. The 32-step run measures a single defect and does not determine its contribution to long-time damping. [Velocity interpolation](../Code/Source/solver/FE/LevelSet/LevelSetKinematicReconciliation.cpp#L277) · [Velocity gather](../Code/Source/solver/FE/LevelSet/LevelSetKinematicReconciliation.cpp#L590) · [Wave generator](../tests/cases/fluid/free_surface_benchmarks/capillary_wave_2d/generate_case.py)

<a id="a02"></a>

### A02. Generalized-α stage pressure is published at the endpoint time

The first-order solver evaluates the mixed residual at tₙ + αf Δt. It reconstructs endpoint differential fields and restores the converged stage values for algebraic fields, including interior pressure. The output writer labels the entire state tₙ₊₁. Consequently a sensor reading this state sees a lag of (1 − αf)Δt for p(t) = t. A prescribed endpoint constraint may overwrite its own DOFs, so free interior and constrained pressure can even represent different times. The stage solution itself is a legitimate quantity. [Stage solve and field reconstruction](../Code/Source/solver/FE/TimeStepping/TimeLoop.cpp#L3126) · [Accepted state and constraints](../Code/Source/solver/FE/TimeStepping/TimeLoop.cpp#L4196) · [Output time](../Code/Source/solver/Application/Core/ApplicationDriver.cpp#L9960) · [Collection timestamp](../Code/Source/solver/Application/Core/ApplicationDriver.cpp#L10380)

In a one-tetrahedron native mixed solve with ∂ₜu = 0 and ∫(p − t)q = 0, at endpoint 0.1 and ρ∞ = 0.5 (αf = 2/3), step sizes 0.1, 0.05 and 0.025 produced p = 0.0666667, 0.0833333 and 0.0916667. The endpoint error is exactly −Δt/3. The capillary-wave, sloshing and oscillating-drop generators use this ρ∞. Expose the stage pressure with its own time or reconstruct an endpoint pressure with the appropriate history and gauge. Validate endpoint constraints, restarts, variable steps, transient traction and integrated impulses. The smooth test establishes the time semantics. It does not measure their contribution to an impact sensor that stays dry. [Jansen, Whiting and Hulbert on generalized-α](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0045-7825(00)00203-6) · [Liu et al. on pressure time placement](https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.01098)

A second native test for A02 imposed physical traction −t n on all four faces of a tetrahedron. With unit density and viscosity, P1 vector velocity, P0 pressure, and natural pressure anchoring, u = 0 and p = t satisfy the transient Stokes equations exactly. Without a prescribed pressure DOF the three pressures reproduced the values above to rounding, and the maximum velocity coefficient was 3.17 × 10⁻¹⁷. This exercises the actual momentum–continuity coupling, normals and traction. It provides a short regression that separates time labeling from a spatial pressure error.

<a id="a03"></a>

### A03. A contact line exactly at a wall vertex loses the strong velocity law

The wall-edge scan accepts opposite, strictly nonzero endpoint signs. When a transversal zero occurs at a shared vertex, neither incident segment passes. In the shipped strip fixture, moving φ from x − 1.3 − 0.2y to x − 1 − 0.2y while preserving its gradient, aggregation and wall-normal Dirichlet condition gave **zero contact samples** and a free tangential DOF. The law gives a tangential speed of 0.696116 in the fixture's sign convention. This can appear intermittently during a time integration and applies when the strong contact-point constraint is selected. Resolve a vertex crossing from the oriented wall neighborhood, distinguish a tangency or an interval of zeros, and install one global constraint. Verify both travel directions and unique ownership on a partition boundary. [Edge predicate](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Constraints/ContactPointVelocityConstraint.cpp#L294) · [Constraint fixture](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Tests/Unit/Constraints/test_ContactPointVelocityConstraint.cpp) · [Ren–E case](../tests/cases/fluid/free_surface_benchmarks/ren_e_2d/generate_case.py#L115) · [Ren and E on contact-line dynamics](https://intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/cms/2011/0009/0002/CMS-2011-0009-0002-a013.pdf)

The direct law constructor also accepts (1,1,0) as an axis-aligned wall normal because each unit component overwrites the selected axis. A nonfinite component alongside a unit component can pass its comparisons. Require exactly one signed unit component and finite zeros in the others. Reachability through deck validation is unverified. [Constructor](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Constraints/ContactPointVelocityConstraint.cpp#L169)

<a id="a04"></a>

### A04. Tetrahedral cut-pressure controls fail with the present stabilization

The fresh configured suite reproduced three failures in the Physics tests that assemble the FE operators. The fixed geometric cut sweep reached 0.408620537516 against a minimum of 0.45. The three-level refinement gave the same minimum and a spread of 1.76440921773 against a maximum of 1.75. The persistent moving cut reached 0.404566509924. The fixtures retain mixed rank. These numbers are the repository's empirical pressure-control criteria. A failed bound alone does not prove a pressure nullspace or an isolated analytical inf-sup constant. [Fixed cuts](../Code/Source/solver/Physics/Tests/Unit/test_FreeSurfaceCutStability.cpp#L10358) · [Three meshes](../Code/Source/solver/Physics/Tests/Unit/test_FreeSurfaceCutStability.cpp#L10645) · [Moving cuts](../Code/Source/solver/Physics/Tests/Unit/test_FreeSurfaceCutStability.cpp#L10840)

The formulation uses the metric in τM and uses 1/(τM tr(G) + ε) in τC. Archived tests on matching meshes isolate the effect. Applying the invariant trace only moved the fixed-cut minimum to about 0.408615. Changing the momentum-time-scale metric only gave 0.461376. The old metric also changed under vertex relabeling. In matched Stokes fields, strengthening the divergence penalty reduced divergence and increased pressure and velocity error. Preserve relabeling invariance and measure all three quantities under h, Δt and cut-position changes before changing a coefficient. Monitor active-space rank, aggregation weights and boundary-pressure convention independently. [Cell metric](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Forms/CellMetric.h) · [VMS coefficients](../Code/Source/solver/Physics/Formulations/NavierStokes/IncompressibleNavierStokesVMSModule.cpp#L193) · [Matched coefficient and relabeling controls](free_surface_program_tracker.md#L2330) · [Massing, Schott and Wall on cut-independent stability](https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.02895) · [Badia, Martín and Verdugo on aggregated mixed spaces](https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.01727)

<a id="a05"></a>

### A05. A four-crossing bilinear quadrilateral can connect the wrong branches

On [−1,1]², φ = xy − 0.2 has four edge roots belonging to two branches. The cutter selects a farthest pair and builds a single segment across branches. Its midpoint has φ = −0.2. The negative area returned was 2.27027027. Direct integration gives 3.043775165. With φ = xy the full zero set has length 4 and the chosen segment has length 2. The modern validated snapshot rejects the first rule against its own certificate, which estimates 3.36. A production path with that validation therefore stops. Direct cutter or volume consumers can receive incorrect geometry. Resolve the bilinear saddle and both branches, or explicitly reject this topology at the cutter. Use both sign choices, rotations and near-saddle perturbations, and integrate both areas independently. Even correct connectivity requires adequate quadrature of the curved branches. [Segment selection](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Interfaces/LevelSetInterfaceBuilder.cpp#L1967) · [Retained quadrature](../Code/Source/solver/FE/LevelSet/LevelSetImplicitCutQuadratureBackend.cpp#L483) · [Nielson and Hamann on ambiguous face connectivity](https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~jrs/meshpapers/NielsonHamann.pdf)

<a id="a06"></a>

### A06. Differentiated cut-surface traction omits motion of the intersection edges

In a unit tetrahedron take φ = x − 1/4, δφ = 1, and sum the P1 test functions in the exterior-pressure form ∫Γ(1 + φ²)nₓ v. Under φ → φ + ε the exact area is (3/4 + ε)²/2. All intersections remain on the same edges. The native residual is 9/32, and regenerated quadrature gives centered derivatives 0.7500000000 at ε = 10⁻⁴, 10⁻⁵ and 10⁻⁶. The contracted assembled tangent is **−2.41 × 10⁻³⁵**. The local curvature term vanishes for this plane while its boundary slides. The existing test perturbs weights with the same curvature formula used by the implementation. Differentiate the regenerated intersections, weights and locations, and compare to independent recuts on planar and curved fixtures. The one-phase SurfaceStress option requires frozen geometry. This defect applies to equations that request the differentiated geometry. [Shape derivative](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Forms/FormKernels.cpp#L16710) · [Tangent assembly](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Forms/FormKernels.cpp#L16930) · [Existing test](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Tests/Unit/Forms/test_CutCellForms.cpp#L775) · [Free-surface option rule](../Code/Source/solver/Physics/Options/NavierStokesOptionRules.cpp#L969) · [Berggren, Theorem 5.2](https://cot.mathres.org/issues/COT202327.pdf)

<a id="a07"></a>

### A07. A generated internal interface computes its parent volume using a surface rule

The generated interior-interface assembly path gives the cell context the interface quadrature, then uses the resulting measure as parent volume. For the same unit tetrahedron and cut, the parent volume is 1/6 and the cut area is 9/32. The specified hₙ = 2Vparent/AΓ is 32/27. Integrating hₙ over the cut should give **1/3**. The assembled value was **0.5625**, twice the cut area. The error changes the viscous μ/hₙ and transient ρhₙ/Δt parts of the internal two-fluid Nitsche penalty in opposite directions. Supply the true physical parent measure using a volume rule or the existing full-cell measure cache. Compare integrated hₙ on translated cuts and under unit scaling on both phases. The witness is for a generated *internal* interface. [Context measure](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Assembly/StandardAssembler.cpp#L7570) · [Generated interface](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Assembly/StandardAssembler.cpp#L11671) · [Penalty consumer](../Code/Source/solver/Physics/Formulations/NavierStokes/NavierStokesBCFactories.h#L1645)

<a id="a08"></a>

### A08. A centroid sign check reverses valid curved fitted boundary normals

Map a Quad9 by F(r,s) = (r, s + 2r²). Its determinant is exactly one everywhere. At the top midpoint the outward normal is +eᵧ. The fitted face routine returned −eᵧ and signed curvature +4 against −4 in the library convention. Quadrature over all four faces gives ∮eᵧ·n ds = **−4**, against zero by the divergence theorem. The centroid can be outside a *local tangent half-space* on a valid curved cell. The ordinary fitted assembler consumes these normals. Use the mapped reference outward covector and the valid map orientation. Check pressure traction, closed flux and orientation permutations. Operators using I − n⊗n are invariant to a sign flip. A curvature vector is likewise unchanged when both signed curvature and normal reverse. [Centroid](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Geometry/FrameGeometry.cpp#L986) · [Sign selection](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Geometry/FrameGeometry.cpp#L1038) · [Fitted assembly](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Assembly/StandardAssembler.cpp#L17682) · [Nanson's surface transformation](https://www.sandia.gov/files/sierra/SM_Theory_5_18/main/stress_measures.html)

### Other completeness and maintenance observations

- The legacy pc_gmres symbol has an empty body. The native vector GMRES route calls gmres_v. A direct caller of the old symbol would perform no solve. Retire it if compatibility permits, or make the unsupported call explicit. [Legacy symbol](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Backends/FSILS/liner_solver/pc_gmres.cpp#L50)
- The Hilbert ordering falls back to a Morton index. It still supplies a permutation, but a Hilbert-specific locality or preconditioner claim requires a different implementation. An old auxiliary-DSL comment calls submodel inclusion a placeholder immediately above the actual slot-remapping implementation. Remove the stale comment and check composed models with distinct state, input and parameter offsets. [Ordering](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Dofs/DofNumbering.cpp#L508) · [Submodel implementation](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Auxiliary/AuxiliaryModelDSL.h#L553)
- Two byte-identical Lagrange performance CSVs contain 900 rows each. The current renderer selects 567 order-sweep and 10 parallel rows. The checked-in summary says 585 source rows and 507 order-sweep rows. Regenerate the summary from the same measured inputs and retain hardware, build and thread metadata. The FE coverage script also prints an under-target warning without returning failure. Its scope is the math test target. [Performance summary](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Basis/performance_graphs/lagrange_performance_summary.txt#L5) · [Renderer](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Basis/performance_graphs/plot_lagrange_performance.py#L67) · [Coverage script](../Code/Source/solver/FE/scripts/run_coverage.sh)
- The book includes topical outlines for the fluid and verification chapters. Neither supplies an executable free-surface verification protocol. The versioned benchmark generators, verifiers and dated evidence in the tracker give the operational definitions. ## Benchmark evidence and tests that separate causes

| Configuration | Evidence and interpretation |
| --- | --- |
| **Fresh tank at rest** | On 2D L8/L16/L32 the maximum nondimensional speeds were 3.54 × 10⁻¹⁴, 1.03 × 10⁻¹³ and 3.14 × 10⁻¹³. On 3D L8/L16 they were 3.39 × 10⁻¹³ and 3.25 × 10⁻¹³. Across all five, the largest normalized pressure error was 5.34 × 10⁻¹⁷. All five reached 100 accepted steps and five sloshing periods. The verifier reported zero relative height and volume drift at saved times and zero total Newton iterations. This exercises constant gravity, atmospheric traction and hydrostatic equilibrium on the initialized state. [Generator](../tests/cases/fluid/free_surface_benchmarks/tank_at_rest/generate_case.py) · [Independent verifier](../tests/cases/fluid/free_surface_benchmarks/tank_at_rest/verify.py) |
| **Fresh moving capillary wave** | Stock one-rank L64, first 32 steps. All 32 were accepted and exactly one reconciliation report reached its limit (A01). A historical U64 trace also recorded limit exhaustion. A 32-step trajectory does not measure four-period damping or frequency error. Compare height and velocity at common times, check each step's signed area budget, and fit a viscous wave reference at the realized amplitude and wavelength. [Wave protocol](../tests/cases/fluid/free_surface_benchmarks/capillary_wave_2d/README.md) · [Denner's capillary-wave analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.08266) |
| **Fitted ALE waves and mesh motion, archived** | On revision 7fd81048c, a four-period wave with 32 cells per wavelength and nondimensional Δt = 0.00055026521435 plus its half/quarter steps gave observed temporal orders of 0.894 for height, 0.575 for liquid velocity and 0.252 for damping. The conservative ALE uniform-flow residual was 1.36 × 10⁻¹⁶, compared with 0.1744 for the default ALE form. Holding the VMS time-scale parameter at the base step in the conservative form gave orders 2.000/2.000/1.997. Pressure sampled at matching stages gave 2.000. The next halving sequence gave 0.921/0.680/0.553 with step-dependent stabilization and 2.000/2.000/1.998 with the fixed scale. On 98c01a500 the revised triangle metric also recovered order two with the fixed scale. A full base-step replay across 98c01a500 and 07e419349 produced 100 byte-identical VTU files. Time refinement with Δt-dependent stabilization changes the spatially discrete operator too. Uniform-flow geometric conservation and pressure time alignment isolate distinct mechanisms. The fixed stabilization parameter is a diagnostic comparison. [Dated study](free_surface_program_tracker.md#L1756) · [Farhat, Geuzaine and Grandmont on geometric conservation](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0021999101969323) |
| **Surface-stress equilibrium, archived and analytical** | At La = 12 the 2D static-drop study reported pressure-jump errors 6.8 × 10⁻⁴, 1.5 × 10⁻⁴ and 3.3 × 10⁻⁵ at R/h = 8/16/32. The surface-stress form γ(I−n⊗n):∇v plus exterior pressure is consistent with the first variation of surface energy. Exact rest also requires the integrated capillary load to lie in the range of the constrained discrete pressure-gradient operator. Compare minₚ ‖fΓ + Gp‖ in a stated velocity dual norm, the pressure jump γ/R (2γ/R for a sphere), peak parasitic capillary number, and volume drift. Even an exactly equilibrated regular inscribed N-gon has perimeter/area derivative ratio 1/[R cos(π/N)]. The pressure-jump error alone cannot identify a forcing or quadrature bug. [Static-drop record](free_surface_program_tracker.md#L1361) · [Surface-stress form](../Code/Source/solver/Physics/Formulations/NavierStokes/NavierStokesBCFactories.h#L1266) · [François et al. on balanced forces](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jcp.2005.08.004) |
| **Ren–E, sessile drops and two-fluid jumps** | A03 targets a strong dynamic endpoint law. In a sessile case also check the imposed angle convention, equilibrium spherical-cap geometry and contact-line dissipation separately. A07 targets an internal Nitsche interface. For a two-fluid static drop measure each phase's pressure, continuous normal velocity and equal/opposite interface work under cut translation and phase exchange. A one-phase atmospheric boundary and an interior two-fluid interface have different operator paths. [Ren–E protocol](../tests/cases/fluid/free_surface_benchmarks/ren_e_2d/README.md) · [Two-fluid method](free_surface_wp10_two_fluid_method.md) |
| **Lobovský dry-bed impact, archived** | The 18.75 mm gated simulation wetted the wall near the observed arrival. Over 0.450–0.470 s the lowest 4.2 mm sensor, spanning 0.9–5.1 mm above the floor, remained dry in the accepted outputs. The predicted impulse was 0 against 105.43 Pa·s measured, while the wet wall above carried substantial pressure. A manufactured divergence-free corner strain on a curved interface had a wall-height error of −10.65 mm on a 20 mm mesh and +0.0449 mm at 0.625 mm at 25 ms. The November replay reproduced the endpoint history after the named-parameter and traction corrections. Measure gap and wetted footprint before and after transport/reconciliation, then pressure on that footprint at its own stage time. A01 and A02 alone do not establish the cause of the missed impulse. [Impact and sensor](free_surface_program_tracker.md#L2286) · [Corner experiment and replay](free_surface_program_tracker.md#L2386) · [Lobovský et al. experimental data](https://arxiv.org/abs/1308.0115) |

**Reference-element controls.** For the canonical Gauss rules on line, triangle, quadrilateral, tetrahedron, hexahedron, wedge and pyramid, 1,589 independent total-degree monomial comparisons through requested degrees 1–7 had maximum absolute error 8.88 × 10⁻¹⁵. Simplex checks used factorial moments, tensor checks used line products and pyramid checks used the shrinking square cross-section. At P1–P4 the same seven Lagrange families reproduced all 638 nodal Kronecker vectors within 3.54 × 10⁻¹⁴. At an interior point in each case the maximum partition, gradient-sum and Hessian-sum errors were 1.89 × 10⁻¹⁵, 4.55 × 10⁻¹⁵ and 1.63 × 10⁻¹³. These controls narrow the search for ordinary affine-scalar cases and make the cut-geometry, cache and specialized-rule counterexamples easier to isolate. [Gauss dispatch](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Quadrature/QuadratureFactory.cpp) · [Lagrange evaluation](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Basis/LagrangeBasis.cpp)

**How to repeat the end-to-end checks.** From the repository root, use the project benchmark Python environment, a Release MPI-enabled svmultiphysics executable, an absolute path in `solver` and an empty output directory in `out`. The native configuration included Eigen, FSILS and LLVM JIT. Give concurrent processes separate JIT cache directories when recording timings. The wave command intentionally reproduces the observed 32-step window.

```bash
base="$PWD/tests/cases/fluid/free_surface_benchmarks"
mkdir -p "$out"
for pair in 2:8 2:16 2:32 3:8 3:16; do
  dim=${pair%:*}
  level=${pair#*:}
  run="$out/tank_${dim}_$level"
  python "$base/tank_at_rest/generate_case.py" --dim "$dim" --level "$level" --output-dir "$run"
  (cd "$run" && mpiexec -n 1 "$solver" solver.xml >solver_run.log 2>&1)
done
python "$base/tank_at_rest/verify.py" "$out"/tank_* --json "$out/tank.json"
run="$out/wave64"
python "$base/capillary_wave_2d/generate_case.py" --level 64 --max-steps 32 --output-dir "$run"
(cd "$run" && mpiexec -n 1 "$solver" solver.xml >solver_run.log 2>&1)
rg 'reconciled_fixed_point_iteration_limit' "$run/solver_run.log"
```

## Verification and coverage

**Scope and provenance.** The inventory contains 1,747 files in 70 directories including the FE root, 1,636 C++ sources/headers totaling 1,012,817 lines and 111 other files. The latter include benchmark assets, figure generators, CMake files, shell scripts and documentation. The checklist records 34,737 named definition sites, including 8,056 GoogleTest definitions in 503 source files, plus 7,285 declaration sites, 6,731 lambdas and 64 function-like macros. Counts are textual source sites. Overloads, conditional alternatives, defaulted/deleted members and repeated line numbers can each occur. Template instantiations in the binary are not additional source definitions.

C++ syntax-tree extraction was reconciled with Universal Ctags and a separate test-macro scan. This recovered functions hidden by argument macros and preprocessor-conditioned constructor signatures. Python functions and lambdas were read from their syntax trees. CMake and shell function definitions were scanned in their own files. File comparisons address the implemented operator, numerical invariant, fixture oracle or supporting artifact. Function groups and call/return observations were generated from source structure to make coverage inspectable. A listed routine has a source-level review record. Only the explicitly named runs and independent probes provide numerical evidence, and suite results give no per-function execution coverage.

**Fresh native suite.** On the ARM64 Release build, 90 of 93 configured CTest entries passed. Three Physics shards failed the FS14 checks in A04. All configured FE CTest entries passed. None of the 93 CTest entries was skipped. Individual GoogleTest cases did skip. The run used Eigen, FSILS, MPI and LLVM JIT. The recorded configuration disables PETSc, Trilinos, MUMPS and the optional DOF test target. All 33 linked executables matched the native-build manifest by SHA-256. Its source commit is 07e419349331b46abc07ee480fd15c030dfc58ca. The FE, Physics and Application directories have no source difference between that commit and the reviewed revision. [Project verification record and manifest references](free_surface_program_tracker.md#L2398) · [DOF build switch](../Code/Source/solver/FE/CMakeLists.txt#L55)

**Additional test sources.** Of 34 test translation units outside the configured compile database, 32 were separately compiled against the native FE interfaces with a GoogleTest entry point. Twenty-five built and exited successfully, one built and reported a failing fixture, and six failed compilation. The other two require the optional Trilinos configuration. The point-evaluation failure was traced to fixture ordering. With the actual cell-to-global DOF map, the same test returned its expected value. This result is separate from the three configured CTest failures.

A local Cppcheck pass screened all 1,636 C++ files using include-stripped copies, selected preprocessor definitions and a local-body warning/portability profile. This deliberately incomplete translation environment produces template, configuration and lifetime false positives. The large Newton file completed on a longer timeout. Its reported temporary at the static vector initializer is returned by value into owned storage. The 21,315-line LLVM generator exceeded the whole-file analysis limit. A follow-up pass completed on its 468 extracted lambda bodies and its enclosing source with nested closures replaced by stubs. This subdivision loses cross-closure dataflow. Native compiled-kernel tests provide independent evidence for the exercised JIT paths. Static warnings alone supply no numerical finding in the tables.

The diagnosis remains bounded by the configurations exercised. The complete current drop, sloshing, two-fluid, fitted-wave and impact release matrices were not rerun. Archived evidence above carries its own revision and measurement protocol. The highest-priority further experiments are a paired wave run after enforcing the returned-geometry volume budget, a time-aligned pressure comparison and a joint pressure/velocity/divergence study on the three failing tetrahedral fixtures.

## File and function checklist

A checked box records that the file was inventoried and compared with its stated numerical or support contract. Each folder opens independently. Source locations use the line at the audited revision. In a function group, an arrow gives a short returned expression or one operation actually called in its body. The group heading names the quantity or contract to interrogate. Declarations are listed separately from bodies. Each lambda is grouped by the operations in its body and indexed by its capture line. Its bound name or a short returned expression is included when available.

For each GoogleTest definition, the entry gives the outcome and one assertion from its body. The assertion favors a numerical check when present. A delegated check has its helper or callable identified where available. A single assertion is an example of the oracle, not the full case. “Passed and skipped” means different invocations of the case had both outcomes. Counts include each source definition across conditional branches.

- [x] [ch01_pdes_and_fem.tex](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Docs/Book/chapters/ch01_pdes_and_fem.tex) — The chapter gives an introduction and a section outline. Weak forms start from a conservation law. Outward surface work and the sign of the pressure gradient determine whether a hydrostatic column balances.

- [x] [ch02_weak_forms_and_galerkin_methods.tex](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Docs/Book/chapters/ch02_weak_forms_and_galerkin_methods.tex) — The chapter gives an introduction and a section outline. Integration by parts fixes the signs of pressure, traction and incompressibility. The constant velocity test reduces a closed boundary term to a flux.

- [x] [ch03_function_spaces_and_well_posedness.tex](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Docs/Book/chapters/ch03_function_spaces_and_well_posedness.tex) — The chapter gives an introduction and a section outline. Trace admissibility, kernels and coercivity determine which boundary and pressure constraints a mixed weak problem admits.

- [x] [ch04_meshes_reference_cells_and_mappings.tex](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Docs/Book/chapters/ch04_meshes_reference_cells_and_mappings.tex) — The chapter gives an introduction and a section outline. The physical gradient uses the inverse transpose. Volume and surface integrals use different Jacobians, as the [A07](#a07) and [A08](#a08) witnesses demonstrate.

- [x] [ch05_finite_elements_and_basis_functions.tex](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Docs/Book/chapters/ch05_finite_elements_and_basis_functions.tex) — The chapter gives an introduction and a section outline. Local interpolation must reproduce polynomial DOFs under orientation. The reference Lagrange tests cover Kronecker values and partition of unity.

- [x] [ch06_interpolation_projection_and_approximation.tex](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Docs/Book/chapters/ch06_interpolation_projection_and_approximation.tex) — The chapter gives an introduction and a section outline. Projection must reproduce a polynomial in the chosen basis. [A17](#a17) gives a warm-cache counterexample for two bases spanning the same space.

- [x] [ch07_numerical_integration_and_element_operators.tex](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Docs/Book/chapters/ch07_numerical_integration_and_element_operators.tex) — The chapter gives an introduction and a section outline. A quadrature exactness claim implies the corresponding monomial moments. The audit integrates 1,589 moments and isolates two nonstandard exceptions in [A22](#a22).

- [x] [ch08_assembly_boundary_conditions_and_constraints.tex](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Docs/Book/chapters/ch08_assembly_boundary_conditions_and_constraints.tex) — The chapter develops the boundary and trace conventions. The text explicitly treats pointwise H1 and vector trace data. The affine lifting identity Pᵀ(b−Ag) gives a check on [A09](#a09).

- [x] [ch09_stability_convergence_and_error_estimation.tex](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Docs/Book/chapters/ch09_stability_convergence_and_error_estimation.tex) — The chapter gives an introduction and a section outline. An observed rate requires a common physical time, norm, mesh family and controlled error sources. The wave and metric controls below demonstrate their importance.

- [x] [ch10_mixed_nonconforming_discontinuous_and_stabilized_methods.tex](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Docs/Book/chapters/ch10_mixed_nonconforming_discontinuous_and_stabilized_methods.tex) — The chapter gives an introduction and a section outline. Mixed velocity–pressure approximation needs stability on the active cut space and compatible constraint treatment. See the three FS14 criteria in [A04](#a04).

- [x] [ch11_eigenvalue_problems_modal_analysis_and_buckling.tex](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Docs/Book/chapters/ch11_eigenvalue_problems_modal_analysis_and_buckling.tex) — The chapter gives an introduction and a section outline. Eigenvalues require a declared norm, pressure gauge and scaling. [A20](#a20) gives two elementary counterexamples to unit/shift independence.

- [x] [ch12_time_dependent_and_nonlinear_problems.tex](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Docs/Book/chapters/ch12_time_dependent_and_nonlinear_problems.tex) — The chapter gives an introduction and a section outline. Time discretization requires correct stage weights, solution epochs and consistent Jacobians. The transient Stokes check [A02](#a02) is independent of spatial error.

- [x] [ch13_architecture_overview.tex](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Docs/Book/chapters/ch13_architecture_overview.tex) — The chapter consists of headings, labels and drafting comments. An architecture diagram must preserve the physics-to-form-to-operator route needed to identify the running formulation.

- [x] [ch14_mesh_library.tex](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Docs/Book/chapters/ch14_mesh_library.tex) — The chapter consists of headings, labels and drafting comments. Mesh connectivity, orientation and ownership must support exact pullbacks and single-counting of boundary faces.

- [x] [ch15_form_language.tex](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Docs/Book/chapters/ch15_form_language.tex) — The chapter consists of headings, labels and drafting comments. The expression language should type pressure, traction and trial/test spaces, then preserve those semantics through differentiation.

- [x] [ch16_form_compiler.tex](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Docs/Book/chapters/ch16_form_compiler.tex) — The chapter consists of headings, labels and drafting comments. The form compiler must produce the same values and directional derivatives as direct quadrature, including geometric terms in [A06](#a06).

- [x] [ch17_jit_compilation.tex](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Docs/Book/chapters/ch17_jit_compilation.tex) — The chapter consists of headings, labels and drafting comments. Generated instructions should reproduce interpreted arithmetic on the same quadrature, history, parameters and cut.

- [x] [ch18_linear_solvers.tex](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Docs/Book/chapters/ch18_linear_solvers.tex) — The chapter consists of headings, labels and drafting comments. A sparse solve should be judged by its true residual and the constrained nullspace of the assembled operator.

- [x] [ch19_parallel_computing.tex](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Docs/Book/chapters/ch19_parallel_computing.tex) — The chapter consists of headings, labels and drafting comments. Parallel execution should agree after ownership reduction, including ghosts, empty ranks and cut surfaces crossing partitions.

Incompressible free-surface reference problems need mass conservation, traction balance, divergence control and matched pressure time.

- [x] [ch21_structural_mechanics.tex](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Docs/Book/chapters/ch21_structural_mechanics.tex) — The chapter consists of headings, labels and drafting comments. For structural terms in coupled problems, rigid translation has zero elastic strain and internal force.

- [x] [ch22_fluid_structure_interaction.tex](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Docs/Book/chapters/ch22_fluid_structure_interaction.tex) — The chapter consists of headings, labels and drafting comments. Fluid and solid must exchange equal and opposite interface work on the same geometry and time stage.

- [x] [ch23_coupled_multiphysics.tex](../Code/Source/solver/FE/Docs/Book/chapters/ch23_coupled_multiphysics.tex) — The chapter consists of headings, labels and drafting comments. Coupled modules require a matched block Jacobian, units and shared interface law.

<a id="fe-inventory-cmake"></a>

### cmake

<details>
<summary>7 files · 2 named definitions</summary>

- [x] [EnableEigen.cmake](../Code/Source/solver/FE/cmake/EnableEigen.cmake) — Discovery and feature defines determine availability of the serial sparse direct comparison used in the hydrostatic benchmark.

- [x] [EnableGTest.cmake](../Code/Source/solver/FE/cmake/EnableGTest.cmake) — Test discovery and imported targets control which numerical checks enter CTest. Source presence alone does not establish execution.

  - **File contract and boundary behavior** · `add_fe_test@73`.

- [x] [EnableLLVMJIT.cmake](../Code/Source/solver/FE/cmake/EnableLLVMJIT.cmake) — The compiler and linked LLVM ABI must match the enabled kernel backend. A fallback run cannot qualify the compiled arithmetic path.

- [x] [EnableMPI.cmake](../Code/Source/solver/FE/cmake/EnableMPI.cmake) — Compile and link flags control which halo and reduction code exists. Single-rank coverage cannot exercise ownership exchange.

  - **Parallel ownership and synchronization** · `add_fe_mpi_test@179`.

- [x] [EnableMUMPS.cmake](../Code/Source/solver/FE/cmake/EnableMUMPS.cmake) — Factorization precision, communicator and integer widths have to agree with the calling FE solver. MUMPS is optional in the test configuration.

- [x] [JITCodegenFingerprint.cmake](../Code/Source/solver/FE/cmake/JITCodegenFingerprint.cmake) — A cache hit must correspond to the same code generator. A changed lowering implementation must invalidate incompatible object code.

- [x] [svfeConfig.cmake.in](../Code/Source/solver/FE/cmake/svfeConfig.cmake.in) — An installed consumer must obtain matching public compile definitions and dependencies, or its view of FE types can differ from the library ABI.

</details>
